visa_intro_1: Credit cards and Bitcoin are both payment systems, but they work very differently.
visa_intro_2: Credit cards like Visa are closed networks controlled by financial institutions, while Bitcoin is an open network that anyone can use.
visa_intro_3: Let's take a look at the differences between these two payment rails: Bitcoin & Visa.
point_1_summary_1: Bitcoin is an open network anyone can join and use without permission. Visa is a closed system controlled by financial institutions that can deny access — especially to the unbanked and underbanked.
point_1_summary_2: This makes Bitcoin more inclusive and accessible to people worldwide, especially those who are unbanked or underbanked.
point_2_summary_1: Bitcoin transactions have no merchant fees. Visa typically charges merchants around 3% per transaction — your business can save money accepting
point_3_summary_1: Every Bitcoin transaction is on a public, auditable blockchain. Visa runs a closed, proprietary system where customers can't independently verify anything.
point_3_summary_2: This transparency makes Bitcoin more trustworthy and allows for independent verification of the network's integrity.
point_4_summary_1: Bitcoin can't be frozen by any central authority. Visa can freeze accounts, block transactions, or deny service at any time.
point_4_summary_2: With Bitcoin, you maintain control over your money and cannot be cut off from the payment system.
point_5_summary_1: Bitcoin is final-settlement — you can only spend what you own. Credit cards create debt with interest rates often over 25% a year.
point_5_summary_2: Bitcoin transactions are final settlements with no debt creation - you can only spend Bitcoin you actually own.
point_6_summary_3: with no bank or payment processor needed. Credit cards always require intermediaries.
point_7_summary_1: Bitcoin works 24/7 globally with no business hours. Visa has operating hours, maintenance windows, and geographic restrictions that can block transactions.
point_7_summary_2: Credit card networks have business hours, maintenance windows, and geographic limitations that can prevent transactions from processing.
